literal: If one dies so that water overflows in the eyes of those who protected them, that death possesses the worthiness of being obtained by begging.
translation: If one can die in such a way that tears well up in the eyes of those who cherished them, such a death is worthy of being sought even by begging.
modern: தம்மைக் காப்பாற்றிய தலைவர்களின் கண்களில் கண்ணீர் பெருகும்படி ஒருவன் இறக்க முடியுமானால், அந்தச் சாவு இரந்து பெற்றுக் கொள்ளத்தக்க தகுதியை உடையதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet extols the ultimate glory of a warrior's death on the battlefield. If a soldier dies fighting so heroically that their commanders or patrons—who nurtured and protected them—shed tears of grief and admiration, that death is the highest honor. The poet suggests that such a meaningful end is so desirable that a warrior should actively beg for it as a boon. The phrase 'புரந்தார்கண் நீர்மல்க' (tears overflowing in the eyes of the protectors) highlights the deep bond of gratitude and duty between the leader and the soldier, making the sacrifice truly noble.
